diagnostics.notes: Both claims concern TRE vs control for body weight. Side A (meta-analysis of 22 RCTs) reports a significant between-group reduction (-0.48 kg, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.22, P<.01). Side B (RESET RCT) reports a per-protocol bodyweight difference of -0.4 kg (-1.8 to 1.0) after follow-up, explicitly 'not maintained', and the authors conclude '3 months of 10-h per-day TRE did not lead to clinically relevant effects on bodyweight'. The extracted fields on both sides match their sources; the B claim correctly targets the follow-up per-protocol estimate with assertion 'not_confirmed'. Comparability is adequate (same exposure class, same outcome, same between-group contrast), though B's claim is the follow-up time point rather than the end-of-intervention point where a small significant per-protocol effect (-1.0 kg, p=0.040) was seen. Since B's authors explicitly conclude no clinically relevant effect / no maintained association against A's reported significant effect, the not_replicated branch applies.

source_evidence.quote: body weight (-0.48 kg, 95% CI: -0.74, -0.22, P < .01) in the TRE intervention group were decreased to varying degrees compared with controls
3 months of 10-h per-day TRE did not lead to clinically relevant effects on bodyweight in middle-aged to older individuals at high risk of type 2 diabetes.

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both findings address TRE versus control for body weight. The meta-analysis (A) reports a significant between-group reduction in body weight with TRE (-0.48 kg, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.22, P<.01). The RESET RCT (B) reports a per-protocol difference of -0.4 kg (-1.8 to 1.0) after follow-up that was 'not maintained', and its authors explicitly conclude that '3 months of 10-h per-day TRE did not lead to clinically relevant effects on bodyweight'. An explicit no-effect/failure-to-confirm conclusion against a reported significant effect places this pair in the not_replicated branch, despite same-sign point estimates.
